To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fura- 2 is an electroactive compound, and that its oxidation is coupled to the uptake of anions across a liquid-liquid interface at pH 7.0.

Fura- 2/AM and its de-esterified form can be reversibly reduced and oxidized in the potential window of 0 to +1.5 V (vs. saturated calomel electrode) in a single step, and that the redox transformations are sensitive to the protonation state of the dye.
the redox transformations of Fura- 2 are not affected by the binding ability toward calcium ions and that Fura- 1 and Fura- 4 do not undergo redox transformations in the pH range from 5 to 8.5.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrochemical properties and transport behavior of Fura- 2/AM and its salt form.
a fundamental understanding of the electrochemical properties and transport behavior of the Ca(2+) indicator Fura-2.
the redox properties of Fura dyes in mimetic biomembranes, and the possible influence of these properties on the Fura-AM-based [Ca(2+)i] measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Fura-3, a derivative of Fura-5, should be used instead of Fura-3/AM for measurements of [Ca2+]i in cells.
the redox transformations of Fura- 2 do not interfere with the [Ca(2+)i] measurements, but the pH and membrane potential do.
Fura- 2/AM is not a redox active species in physiological conditions and thus does not interfere with [C2+]i measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Fura- 2/AM can be used to mimic the transport across a lipophillic barrier, while Fura-2 itself can be used to measure [Ca(2+) ](i) in the cytosol.
Fura- 2 is a redox-active compound which is able to transport ions across a liquid-liquid interface, and which is able to undergo a reversible redox reaction.
Fura-1, Fura-2, and Fura-5 are all redox active in a pH-dependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fura- 2 is a versatile redox-active probe that can be used to study the transport of ions across liquid-liquid and liquid-lipid interfaces.

Fura- 2/AM is a redox-active molecule and its redox reactions are sensitive to changes of the local pH, membrane potential and Ca(2+), and thus should be taken into account in the analysis of the [Ca(2)](i) concentration in living cells.
Fura-1 and Fura-4F are more suitable for redox transformations than Fura-2.
